refs: Blumgart Surgery of the Liver 6e Ch 89 and Ch 75

steps.say: Cavernous haemangioma is the commonest benign liver tumour and usually an incidental finding. Contrast CT shows peripheral nodular enhancement filling toward the centre over time. Giant symptomatic lesions over ten centimetres need enucleation.
steps.tx: **Cavernous haemangioma** shows peripheral nodular enhancement with **centripetal fill-in** on contrast CT, and giant **symptomatic** lesions over **10** cm need enucleation. Small asymptomatic lesions need no follow-up imaging once characterised, while pain, growth or diagnostic doubt pushes toward resection. Enucleation along the compressed pseudocapsule bleeds less than formal hepatectomy for these vascular tumours.

steps.say: Focal nodular hyperplasia is the benign lesion with a central scar and spoke wheel vessels. Liver function stays normal, so management is observation alone. Biopsy only when adenoma cannot be excluded, since the scar can be hard to see.
steps.tx: **Focal nodular hyperplasia** shows a **central scar** with radiating septa and normal liver function, managed by observation with biopsy only when adenoma cannot be excluded. Hepatobiliary contrast MRI typically retains dye in functioning FNH while most adenomas wash out, settling most dilemmas without a needle. Oral contraceptives need not stop, and malignant transformation essentially never happens in true FNH.

vis.alt: CT and MRI of focal nodular hyperplasia showing spoke-wheel arterial pattern, delayed scar enhancement and hepatobiliary contrast retention.
vis.caption: FNH spoke-wheel scar across phases. Image: StewardMD.

steps.say: Hepatocellular adenoma is the benign tumour that can bleed and turn malignant. Resect lesions over five centimetres, beta catenin mutated subtypes and any adenoma in a man. Stop oral contraceptives at diagnosis and re-image in six months; small lesions in women often shrink.
steps.tx: **Hepatocellular adenoma** over **5** cm, **beta-catenin** mutated subtype or male sex needs resection because of bleeding and malignant transformation risk, and oral contraceptives must stop. Inflammatory and HNF1a subtypes behave better, though inflammatory lesions still bleed, but beta-catenin activation carries real cancer risk even when small. MRI with hepatobiliary contrast plus biopsy classifies the subtype, and men proceed to resection regardless of size.

steps.say: Simple liver cysts with thin walls and no enhancement are harmless and need no follow up. Dominant symptomatic cysts over ten centimetres get laparoscopic fenestration with omental packing. Wide deroofing stops the cyst resealing.
steps.tx: **Simple cyst** with thin walls and no enhancement are observed, while symptomatic dominant cysts over **10** cm get laparoscopic **fenestration** with omental packing. Deroof the dome widely so the remaining cavity drains freely into the peritoneum, and pack omentum to prevent reclosure. Complex septated or mural-nodular cysts break this rule and need complete excision as possible mucinous neoplasms once hydatid is excluded.

steps.say: Polycystic liver replaces parenchyma with many non communicating cysts while function stays preserved. Gigot type two with dominant cysts suits fenestration, while diffuse type three with intractable symptoms needs transplant evaluation. Treat the symptom burden, not the scan appearance.
steps.tx: **Polycystic liver** disease with **Gigot** type **II** dominant cysts suits fenestration, while diffuse type **III** with intractable symptoms needs transplantation evaluation. Massive hepatomegaly compresses stomach, diaphragm and vena cava despite normal liver function tests. Fenestrate dominant anterior cysts for pressure relief, and reserve combined liver-kidney listing for type III with renal failure or unbearable mass effect.

vis.alt: Polycystic liver with multiple non-communicating biliary cysts and histology showing ductal plate malformation with von Meyenburg complex.
vis.caption: Polycystic liver with von Meyenburg complex. Image: StewardMD.

steps.say: Von Meyenburg complexes are tiny bile duct hamartomas under five millimetres and need no follow up. Mucinous cystic neoplasms look similar but carry septations and need complete resection. Size plus septations separate the innocent from the dangerous.
steps.tx: Biliary hamartomas under 5 mm as **von Meyenburg** complexes are incidental and need no follow-up, unlike **mucinous cystic neoplasms** with septations that need complete resection. Mucinous cystic tumours show ovarian-type stroma, occur in middle-aged women and rarely communicate with the duct. Any septated cystic lesion over 5 cm with mural nodules leaves surveillance and goes to formal resection.

steps.say: Peliosis fills the liver with blood filled cavities from steroids or Bartonella infection. Drug-induced cases regress when the drug stops, and Bartonella peliosis needs antibiotics, while adenoma is a true neoplasm. Stop the cause first and watch the cavities regress.
steps.tx: **Peliosis** from steroids or Bartonella shows **blood-filled cavities**; drug-induced cases reverse on withdrawing the drug, unlike adenoma which is a true neoplasm. Anabolic steroids, oral contraceptives and immunosuppression head the drug list, and Bartonella peliosis accompanies bacillary angiomatosis in immunocompromise. Biopsy shows blood lakes without neoplastic cells, and rupture with haemoperitoneum is the feared complication of missed cases.

steps.say: Hepatic angiomyolipoma declares itself with fat density and HMB-45 positivity. Small certain lesions stay under observation, and resection waits for diagnostic doubt or growth beyond five centimetres. Fat on imaging is a reassuring clue when present, since many AMLs are fat-poor.
steps.tx: Hepatic **angiomyolipoma** with fat density and **HMB-45** positivity is observed when small, and resection is reserved for diagnostic doubt or growth over **5** cm. Epithelioid variants behave more aggressively and lower the resection threshold, while classic triphasic tumours with vessels, muscle and fat usually stay indolent. Biopsy proves HMB-45 when imaging overlaps with adenoma or carcinoma, since fat alone does not exclude malignancy.
